text:
Alex: Quick flag — we're seeing a mismatch between hosted API demand and our committed GPU supply projection for next quarter. Need to decide if we buy another reserved tranche or rely on on-demand bursts.

Priya: How big is the gap? rough numbers please. finance needs cost delta to compare against overage charges and committed discounts. :eyes:

Alex: Current committed = 320 GPU-equivalents across us-west1 + eu-central1. Forecasted steady-state demand (hosted API) = ~380 GPU-equivalents at 95th pct, with spikes to ~460 during peak new-feature rollout windows.

Mateo: Utilization telemetry agrees — long-tail sessions and increased chat workloads pushed avg tokens/sec up ~18% last month. Cluster fill is already 88% in us-west during peak.

Lin: Region constraint: us-west1 is our densest pool and nearly saturated for A100 rentals. eu-central1 has some spare but network egress for cross-region KV cache sync would add latency. We can shift stateless workloads but not pinned-cache inference without warm-up.

OpsBot: nightly-cluster-report: clusters: 5 pools, committed: 320 GPUs, on-demand capacity available: 120 GPUs, 7 incidents last 30d (capacity saturation alerts).

Jenna: Product note — Canary for new embeddings-heavy feature rolls out in 3 weeks; expected to add ~35-50 GPUs worth of sustained load in the first 10 days if adoption follows the internal beta.

Priya: Cost fallback comparison? commit vs on-demand vs spot? we need monthly delta. Also want committed term options: 1yr vs 3yr.

Alex: Quick back-of-envelope: 320 reserved at current pricing = $380k/month (commit cost). Incremental on-demand for 60 GPUs at peak ~ $90k/month. If we buy +40 reserved (to hit 360) monthly comms move to ~$425k, but on-demand overage drops to ~20 GPUs ($30k). Numbers simplified — need billing export to be precise.

Mateo: Also consider SLO risk: if we rely on on-demand bursts we see 150-300ms extra cold-start tail on some requests during supply juggling. That degrades latency SLO; product won't be happy.

Lin: Two options: 1) Buy 40-60 GPU reserved in us-west and eu split (to avoid cross-region latency). 2) Keep reserve as-is, add autoscaling policies for on-demand with pre-warm windows and increase KV cache TTL to reduce hot-path GPU usage.

Omar: Cloud ops note — procurement lead time for reserved instances varies by provider and instance type; some vendors need 7-14 days to confirm capacity for 100+ GPUs. If we decide to commit, we should start procurement now to hit 'in-market' before Canary.

Priya: Action item from finance: run two scenarios in the next 48h: A) +40 GPUs reserved (1yr) B) No new reserves but model 20% on-demand average for spikes. Include expected invoice delta and committed discount amortized.

Alex: I'll put together utilisation slices per region and peak-hour heatmaps. Mateo, can you extract the request-level tail latencies for the last 30 days tied to saturation events?

Mateo: On it. I'll paste a short snippet here when ready.

(10m later) Mateo: snippet: ```sql
-- high-level query
SELECT hour, avg_gpu_util, p95_latency_ms, incidents
FROM infra.metrics
WHERE metric='gpu_util' AND ts >= '2026-02-01'
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 72;
```

Priya: Also include committed purchase options pricing from cloud vendor portal. If 3yr saves >25% over 1yr + on-demand risk, that's attractive but we need forecast confidence.

Jenna: Small ask — can we guarantee a small reserved pool for the Canary region (eu-central) so we don't blow the experiment? 20 GPUs would be enough for staged rollout.

Alex: Proposal: short-term safety buy: 20 GPUs reserved in eu-central (1yr) to protect Canary + 20 GPUs reserved in us-west (1yr) to reduce SLO risk. Model remaining spikes with controlled on-demand bursts and tighter cache policies.

Omar: Confirmed vendor availability for small tranche ~20 GPUs in eu-central; will need PO and spending approval.

Priya: I'll draft the cost comparison spreadsheet and run the model. Expect initial numbers in ~36h. If we need to act faster, let me know.

Lin: If finance approves the split-reserve, platform can stage the rollout and pin the Canary to eu-central reserved pool. We'll add routing policy so Canary traffic never leaves eu-central.

Alex: Cool. Final ask: please post the billing export link and the 72h util plots here when available. We'll reconvene once Feb-to-Mar billing is parsed. :thumbsup:

Omar: Leaving a note — if procurement lags, fallback is cross-project spot pool which has higher preemption risk but cheaper cost. Documented in runbook: `infra/runbooks/gpu_comms.md`

Priya: Thanks all — I'll follow up with a formal commit recommendation after modeling.

Mateo: Added a quick graph to the infra dashboard: /dashboards/gpu-utilization?q=hosted-api — helps visualize live heatmaps.

Alex: Thanks team. We'll aim to decide by EOD Wednesday to hit vendor windows.
